pr_title: Escape liquid tags in site docs
pr_body:
It is good practice to wrap all dynamic content in `{% raw %}..{% endraw %}` Liquid tags so that no syntax within can mistakenly get interpreted as Liquid tags. Fixes rendering of `gh auth login` help page.

Fixes https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/6149

issue_context.title: Manual: Small fix in manual on gh auth login page
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

The `gh auth login` [page](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_auth_login) has a small bug:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/19912012/186936477-e3f58a4e-f010-430d-ac84-9d0d0cea386d.png)

The line in the docs needs to be wrapped in the `{% raw %}` and `{% endraw %}` tags.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

See: https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_auth_login

### Expected vs actual behavior

It should say:

> To use gh in GitHub Actions, add `GH_TOKEN: ${{secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN}}` to "env".

### Logs

n/a
comments:
I think `go run ./cmd/gen-docs --website` generates `gh_auth_login.md` correctly:

```
...
Alternatively, gh will use the authentication token found in environment variables.
This method is most suitable for "headless" use of gh such as in automation. See
`gh help environment` for more info.

To use gh in GitHub Actions, add `GH_TOKEN: ${{secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN}}` to "env".
...
```

@samcoe Maybe the problem is about how `github/cli.github.com` renders the templates.

@nsmag That is correct, it is a rendering issue not necessarily a generation issue. The recommended solution is to wrap that line in `{% raw %}` and `{% endraw %}` tags so that `{{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` does not get interpreted when being rendered. That is easy enough to add but then those `raw` tags causes an issue when outputting the text on the commands line. That is what makes this a bit more tricky to fix.

review_comments: Seems like it would be a bit simpler if we just move this end tag down to line 129 and remove the `raw` tags from the example section, that way this whole function would just be wrapped in `raw` tags.
The only gotcha is that then the intentional `{% highlight bash %}` liquid tag in the Examples section wouldn't work
Ah I missed that, ignore my comment then.
